transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I… I guess I came because I can’t shake this feeling—no, it feels more certain than a feeling—that I’m being punished for letting my father decline. My sister keeps showing me the doctor’s notes and saying I did everything I was supposed to do, and she’s always been the organized one, she keeps folders for everything… but it doesn’t change it. It feels like some judgment has already been passed on me, like it’s too late to argue my side.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things, even when others tell you it’s not your fault?

Yes… all the time. I keep replaying every appointment I made for my father, every time I didn’t push hard enough, or maybe pushed too much, and then the conversations with my relatives—my aunt has this way of sighing before she says anything, like she’s already disappointed, she used to do that at Thanksgiving too—and I just end up thinking I must be selfish. Like I failed as a daughter.

And then at work, I’ll make some small mistake or even just fall behind on an email, and it feels like proof that I’m useless there too. Like I deserve whatever happens after that.
Do these feelings of guilt or self-blame happen even when you haven’t done anything specific that you can point to, or do they always seem to tie back to something you think you did or didn’t do?

It usually ties itself to something, I think… like my father’s appointments, every decision I made or didn’t make. I keep going back over them, and then those tense conversations with my relatives—my cousin still barely looks at me at family things, though maybe that’s just how she is, she was like that at my niece’s graduation too—and it all turns into this… conclusion that I’m selfish, that I was a bad daughter.

And then it spreads. Like at work, if I miss something small, suddenly it feels like I’m not just behind, I’m useless. Like I deserve whatever comes next.
Do these feelings of guilt and self-blame show up in other areas of your life, or do they mostly center around your father’s care and family interactions?

It starts with my father, mostly… the appointments, the things I should’ve asked, every decision I made. And then I’ll think about those tense talks with my relatives—my aunt’s comments, my cousin not really looking at me—and it all turns into this idea that I’m a selfish daughter.

But it doesn’t stay there. At work, if I miss something or don’t answer fast enough, I feel like that proves I’m useless too. Like I deserve whatever happens after that.
Have these feelings of guilt and self-blame been happening almost every day, and do you feel like they’ve really changed how you’re able to function at work or with your family?

Yes… it feels like almost every day. I’ll be at work and I’m supposed to be handling something simple, like an employee form or an email, and instead my mind goes right back to my father’s appointments—what I should’ve asked, whether I chose the wrong time, whether I missed something obvious. Then I start thinking about the conversations with my relatives, the tense ones, and it’s like it all becomes proof that I’m selfish.

And then at work, if I’m slow or make a small mistake, I don’t just think, “I made a mistake.” I think, “Of course, I’m useless here too.” Like I deserve whatever happens. With family, I avoid things or I get so stuck trying to say the right thing that I barely say anything. So yes… it’s changed things. I’m not functioning the way I used to.
Have you noticed that most days, you feel down or lose interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?

Yes… most days. I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling, like everything has sort of lost its color. Even things I used to care about don’t really reach me.

I’ll be sitting at my desk in HR, looking at work I know I should be able to do, or I’ll go out and stare at the garden beds—because I used to like that, the planting and weeding—and it’s like I’m just looking through glass. It’s there, but I can’t feel anything from it.
Have these symptoms of depression been present continuously for at least two years, or have there been periods when you felt better for a while before they came back?

Not two years, no… at least I don’t think so. It’s been about a year and maybe two months now.

It really started when my father’s health and behavior began changing, and I had to step in more with caregiving. Before that, I had stress, sure, everyone does, but it wasn’t like this constant thing. Since then it’s just kind of… stayed. Like everything got pulled into that one situation and never really went back.

Have your feelings of depression, like feeling down or losing interest in things, been present non-stop for at least two years, or have there been clear times when you felt significantly better for a while?

Not two years, no. It’s been more like… about a year and two months, I think.

It started around when my father’s health and his behavior began changing, and I had to step in more, with appointments and caregiving and all of that. I keep thinking about that period, because everything kind of shifted then. Before that I had bad days, of course, but not like this. Since then it hasn’t really let up.
Before this current period of feeling down and losing interest in things, have you ever had a time when you felt this way for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so… not like this, not for two weeks in a row before. I mean, I’ve had rough patches—work stress, family things, you know, normal life—but this current stretch is the one that’s just stayed.

It’s been about a year and two months now, since my father’s health and behavior started changing and I had to step into the caregiving role more. That’s when it really began, and it hasn’t felt like it lifted in any real way since.
During this current time when you’ve been feeling down and losing interest in things, have you had even a few days when your mood felt clearly better, even for a short while?

Not really… I mean, maybe there are moments where I’m distracted, like if something urgent comes up at work, but I wouldn’t say my mood feels clearly better.

Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It’s like the color has gone out of everything. I can be sitting at my desk in HR, answering emails, or even looking out at the garden beds at home—something I used to notice more—and it just doesn’t reach me. It’s all sort of flat.
During this time when you’ve been feeling down, have you had any days where your mood suddenly felt much better, almost high, or where you had a lot more energy than usual?

I don’t think so… I mean, I’m not sure what would count as “high.” I haven’t noticed suddenly feeling great or like I had all this extra energy.

Sometimes I’ll get moving if there’s something I absolutely have to handle, like a work thing, and then I sort of look busy from the outside, but it doesn’t feel like I’m suddenly better. It’s more like I’m just pushing through because the email has to be answered or the call has to be made. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had days like that.
Have you experienced a period where your sadness felt more like grief over your father’s condition or decline, rather than a general depressed mood that affects most areas of your life?

I mean… yes and no. My father is part of it, of course. When I think about how he’s changed, it hurts in a very specific way, like grief, I guess.

But it doesn’t stay neatly in that box. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, and it’s like the color has gone out of everything. I can be at my desk in HR, just staring at an email, or at home looking at the garden beds—plants I used to care about—and it’s like none of it really reaches me anymore.

So… it’s not just when I’m thinking about him. It feels more spread out than that.
Have there been any periods lasting at least a few weeks when you felt clearly better and returned to your usual self, even if it didn’t last very long?

No… I don’t think there’s been a stretch of a few weeks where I felt like myself again.

It’s been going on for… about a year and two months now, I think. Since my father’s health and behavior started changing and I had to step into more of the caregiving stuff. At first I kept thinking it was just that situation, like once I got things organized or got used to it, I’d come back around. I even bought a new planner—one of those overly detailed ones with tabs—and I remember thinking if I could just schedule everything properly, maybe I’d feel more normal.

But it hasn’t really lifted like that. There might be an hour here or there where I’m distracted, but not weeks where I’m back to my usual self.
